entries.reason: The MCP server's pages allow no script (default-src 'none') and load images only as data: URLs, so injected CSS can neither run code nor fetch or send anything. The inline style is each page's own stylesheet.

No form-action on purpose (web/mcp/pages/index.ts htmlResponse): Chrome applies it to the redirect after the consent form's POST, which goes to the AI app's own callback. The pages allow no script, and their templates escape every value a request can carry (quality-speed/pages/security/PLAN.md, the audits).

ZAP looks for a token by name only. The consent form carries the OAuth library's consent handle: single-use, 10 minutes, tied to the browser that opened it (web/mcp/authorize.ts). The /connect form downloads the Copilot package and changes nothing.

The scan reaches the Workers over plain HTTP on localhost by design. A deployed room runs on a Cloudflare custom domain, which serves HTTPS, and the room sends HSTS for a year (web/worker/headers.ts).

The scan's script string comes back as JSON data (application/json, nosniff, CSP default-src 'none'). The room's pages put comment bodies in with textContent and el(), never innerHTML (web/src/scripts/comments.ts).

False positive. `reason` is a bound parameter (?4 in web/worker/hold.ts releaseHold); the two responses differ because the first request releases the hold, so the second finds none and returns another status.

False positive. `name` is a bound parameter (?3 in web/worker/hold.ts addCustodian); the two responses differ because the first request adds the custodian, so the second adds none (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) and returns another status.

The scan's script string comes back as JSON data (application/json from Response.json in web/worker/http.ts; nosniff and CSP default-src 'none' from web/worker/headers.ts). The hold page puts the notice and custodians in with textContent and el(), never innerHTML (web/src/scripts/hold.ts).
The Unix times are RFC 7591's client_id_issued_at in /register answers and numeric constants in the build's script files. Neither says anything about the room.

The address in the URL is the crawler's own invented one, which it typed into the Activity filter and the hold page's forms. The room sends Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, so a URL never leaves for another site.

Informational. The query values ZAP matched (action=sign_in, view=decided) are the filters' own fixed option values. The room serves these pages as files built ahead of time and never writes a query value into them.
Informational: the pages use script, so ZAP suggests its browser-driven spider. The room's route table, imported as an API definition, covers every route the pages call.

Informational: ZAP notes a response that sets a cookie it takes for a session token. It is the forms' anti-forgery token (web/mcp/forms.ts) or the OAuth library's consent cookie, and names no weakness.
Informational: ZAP lists answers that differ when it changes the User-Agent header. Neither Worker decides access by User-Agent; the room only records it in its audit log.

ZAP sent the route's own last segment as a custodian's name and saw a different answer. The name is a D1 bound parameter (web/worker/hold.ts addCustodian) and a Worker has no file system; the answer flips between 201 and 409 because a custodian is added once per hold.

ZAP sent the route's own last segment (release) as the reason and saw a different answer. The reason only reaches a D1 bound parameter (?4 in web/worker/hold.ts releaseHold), never a file, R2 key, fetch or redirect, and a Worker has no file system; the answer flips because the first request releases the hold and later ones get 409 no_hold (web/worker/routes/hold.ts step).
Informational. The match is the word select in a minified MCP App view's own script (this.select(t)), sent in a POST /mcp resource, not a comment. It names no table or query.
